definition.en-US: The list of what a project will do and what it will leave out for now.

analogy.en-US: Like packing for a weekend trip, where you choose what fits in the bag and leave the rest at home.

definition.en-US: A written description of what an app must do, who uses it and what it must never do.

analogy.en-US: Like a recipe card that lists the dish to make, the ingredients to use and the steps that must never be skipped.

definition.en-US: A list of statements that are each either true or false when you test the app, and that are all true when the first version is finished.

analogy.en-US: Like a packing list that you tick off at the door, where the trip is ready only when every line is ticked.

definition.en-US: A separate line of work in a repository, so that changes can be made and tested without changing the main version.

analogy.en-US: Like a draft copy of a document that you edit on the side, while the signed original stays in the drawer.

definition.en-US: A request to bring the changes from one branch into another branch after other people have read them.

analogy.en-US: Like handing a finished homework page to a teacher for marking before it goes into the class folder.

definition.en-US: A key, password or token that gives access to a service or an account, and that must never appear in a public file.

analogy.en-US: Like the spare key under the doormat, because anyone who finds it can open the door.

definition.en-US: A monthly cap on what a paid service may charge you, which stops requests or warns you when the cap is reached.

analogy.en-US: Like a prepaid phone plan that stops calls when the credit runs out, instead of letting the bill keep growing.

definition.en-US: Putting a finished version of your app on a server where other people can open it at an address.

analogy.en-US: Like moving a finished painting from the studio to the gallery wall, where visitors can see it.

definition.en-US: A text file at the front of a project that tells visitors what it is, why it is useful and how to use it.

analogy.en-US: Like the label on a jar, which tells you what is inside, what it is for and how to open it.

definition.en-US: A small collection of your best finished work, shown so that other people can judge what you have made.

analogy.en-US: Like a photo album you hand to a new neighbour so they can see what you did last summer.

definition.en-US: A check of a proposed change by another person, who leaves comments and then approves the change or asks for changes.

analogy.en-US: Like a second reader who checks an essay for mistakes before it is handed in.

definition.en-US: A stop in merging that happens when two branches change the same part of a file, so that Git cannot choose between the two versions.

analogy.en-US: Like two friends editing the same sentence in a shared document, so someone has to decide which words stay.

definition.en-US: A rule on an important branch that controls who can change it and what must happen before a change is accepted, such as a review.

analogy.en-US: Like a museum rule that a painting can only be moved after two staff members sign the form.

definition.en-US: A short review of a finished project that records what went well, what went wrong and what to change next time.

analogy.en-US: Like a coach who watches the match video after the game to decide what the team should practise next.

definition.en-US: The list of saved checkpoints in a repository, showing what changed in each one and when it was saved.

analogy.en-US: Like the list of saved versions of a document, which shows each time someone pressed save.
